about: How long pairtime keeps each kind of data, from DESIGN 4.4. This file is the one copy the code reads. The privacy notice at /privacy renders its retention table from it, and pairtimed's retention jobs take their periods, tables and columns from it. In kept, {days} stands for the entry's days and {window} for the spot-check window, so a number is never written twice. Every table pairtimed's migrations create belongs to an entry or is listed in no_personal_data. An entry with a period (days or {window}) puts each of its tables under one of its jobs, which deletes its rows on time, or in lifetime_tables when its rows stay while the account exists; only an entry without a period lists plain tables. A hold's table is also the table of one of its entry's jobs by the window, which deletes the hold rows once their spot-check window has closed. An evidence entry's jobs stay off until WP-SV18, which deletes the blob each row names before the row. A job or hold with awaits set is off until the work package named there creates its table, and that package removes awaits.

spot_check_window.provisional: DESIGN 4.4 and 13.2 item 4: 12 months after the decision until Hack Club HQ sets the spot-check window

entries.data: The text of your prompts, and the agent's final reply to each one
entries.kept: {days}, or until a submission that covers them is decided, whichever is later. You can shorten this, or turn off "keep prompt text"

entries.data: Your AI tool's transcripts and output
entries.kept: Not copied: pairtime reads them where your AI tool keeps them. What the tool hands pairtime itself, through its hooks, waits on this computer until the agent has read it: in pairtime's inbox while the agent isn't running or doesn't answer in time, and as the hook calls listed below. Everything else follows the tool's own setting (Claude Code keeps them for 30 days unless you change it)

entries.data: File paths kept for your recaps, and the commands your agent ran
entries.kept: {days}

entries.data: Presence and focus samples, typing counts if you turned on the typing module, and prompt similarity sketches (MinHash), which pairtime keeps inside the ledger's records
entries.kept: With the ledger records that hold them: {days}, or longer while a submission that uses them is inside its spot-check window ({window})

entries.data: Ledger records and batch roots: the sealed log of what pairtime recorded
entries.kept: {days}, or longer while a submission that uses them is inside its spot-check window ({window}). While this computer is linked, the batch roots of online batches that haven't reached the server yet stay, without their records, until the server has them, unless a fork or the server's device_mismatch has ended the chain

entries.data: Minute buckets
entries.kept: {days}. Daily totals and coach records stay until you delete them

entries.data: Hook calls the agent hasn't read yet: what your AI tool sent pairtime as you worked, which can be your prompts, its replies, the commands it ran with their output, and the files it edited. They're plain text, not encrypted, in a folder other people's accounts on this computer can't open, though an administrator can
entries.kept: Until the agent has read them, and {days} at most. Once the ledger can't open until you run pairtime restore, no new call is kept

entries.data: The inbox: what your AI tool sent pairtime while the agent wasn't running or didn't answer in time. That can be your prompts, its replies, the commands it ran with their output, and the files it edited. It's plain text, not encrypted, in a folder other people's accounts on this computer can't open, though an administrator can
entries.kept: Until the agent has read it, and {days} at most after it was written. Once the ledger can't open until you run pairtime restore, nothing new waits there

entries.data: Commit records: for each commit pairtime sees in your projects, its ID and its parents, its times, how many files and lines changed, which commits it replaced if you rebased or amended, and whether an AI agent made it, with no commit message and no file name
entries.kept: {days}

entries.data: A record of each upload the server answered: when, to which server, how many batch roots, minute buckets and commit records it carried and whether it carried the labels, the codes in the server's answer, and a hash of what was sent, never what was sent itself. The same for each request that turned a project's name on or off on your dashboard, answered or not: how many names it carried and a hash, never the names themselves
entries.kept: {days}

entries.data: What the server last told this computer about your project names: the name your dashboard shows for each project you turned a name on for, the short code your dashboard calls each project by, when the server answered, which names you hid on your dashboard, the names pairtime sent and the projects it asked the server to stop naming since the server last answered, until an answer settles them, and a note of each name pairtime turned off because your dashboard doesn't show it, with its name and when pairtime found it
entries.kept: The server's last answer until its next one replaces it. A note until your dashboard shows that name again after you turned it on, the oldest notes going first when there are very many. Only the notes stay when this computer signs in to another server. All of it until you uninstall pairtime or delete everything

entries.data: The project map: for each git repo you worked in, its folder, its project's key and the commits its history starts from, and for each folder you worked in, when pairtime last saw it. A folder that isn't a git repo is kept only as a key made from its path, never the path
entries.kept: A repo's folder until pairtime finds another repo, or none, where it was. A folder's key a day after pairtime last saw the folder, unless the folder got a new project key because the repo that was there is gone. The rest until you uninstall pairtime or delete everything

entries.data: Your device key
entries.kept: Until you uninstall pairtime or the key is replaced

entries.data: Your account: your Hack Club Auth ID, Slack ID and handle, your email address (stored encrypted, with a keyed hash so a deletion request can find it), whether Hack Club Auth has verified you and says you're eligible for its programs, when you signed up and last signed in, the time zone your dashboard counts your days in, with the time of each change you made to it and the zone it changed from, your GitHub user ID if you link GitHub, and, if you volunteer for the scoring's calibration, that an operator marked your account for it and since when, until the calibration ends
entries.kept: While your account exists

entries.data: Sign-in sessions: for each browser you sign in with, a hash of its session cookie (never the cookie itself), when you signed in, when Hack Club Auth last checked it was you, and the first name Hack Club Auth gave at that sign-in, which the pages show as who's signed in
entries.kept: Until you sign out, or 30 days after you sign in at the latest. The record is deleted 1 day after the session ends

entries.data: Your devices: for each computer you link with pairtime login, a random device ID, a hash of its sign-in token (never the token itself), the public key that signs its uploads, the OS family, the pairtime build, when you linked it, when it last connected and when you removed it, how many times it has been linked, how far its uploads have got (the number of its last upload, the number, hash and arrival time of the last batch root it sent, the batch its record starts at, and the numbers of the batches it kept to itself in local-only mode between two sign-ins), and the labels its uploads carry: the names and versions of your AI tools, the scoring version and parameter hash, whether the typing module is on, and whether pairtime thinks it runs in a virtual machine
entries.kept: Until you remove the device. Then its device ID, when you removed it, how many times it has been linked and how far its uploads have got stay {days} more, or as long as this server keeps anything the device uploaded, if that's longer. Everything else about the device goes at once, except its pairtime build and the other labels its uploads carry, which stay until {days} after the device last sent them. A device removed before it uploaded anything is deleted at once

entries.data: Codes for linking a computer: a hash of the code you type and of the app's own code, the device ID, OS family, pairtime build and public key the app sent, when the app asked for the code and when it last checked on it, and which account approved or turned it down, and when
entries.kept: The code works for 15 minutes after the app asks for it. The record is deleted 1 day after that

entries.data: The IP address each upload comes from, and its TLS fingerprint (JA4)
entries.kept: {days}, then deleted outright, not shortened

entries.data: Minute buckets: for each 15 seconds, the credited seconds by project key, why they were credited and what kind of work they counted as, with the reasons for seconds that weren't credited, how long an AI agent was running, for each project key how long an AI agent ran there without you getting credit there, and the project each of your devices' project keys counts toward
entries.kept: Per-minute detail for {days}, the furthest back a submission can reach. Minutes a submission uses stay until its spot-check window closes ({window}). After that only daily totals per project and kind of work, split by evidence level, the time your agent worked on its own in each project, and the project each of your devices' project keys counts toward, stay for as long as your account exists

entries.data: Witness rows and batch roots: the hash of each upload batch, and when the server received it; the hashes behind each day root, one for each batch the server received that day, from which it proves that a batch arrived that day; and for each computer the server's answer to its latest upload, which a retry of that upload gets again
entries.kept: {days}. Rows that a submission uses stay until its spot-check window closes ({window}). The hashes behind a day root stay as long as any of that day's batch records do, yours among them after you delete your account, since taking one out would break the proofs of the day's other batches

entries.data: Commit records (commit IDs, times and line counts, with file paths only as keyed hashes), project fingerprints, and the pushes pairtime's GitHub App reports if you install it
entries.kept: While your account exists

entries.data: The names of your projects you chose to show on your own dashboard: for each one, the label you approved on your computer, the device and project key it names, when the server got it, and when you removed that device, if you did. Only your own dashboard shows them
entries.kept: Until you turn the name off on your computer or hide it on your dashboard, either of which deletes it at once. After a hide, only the project key and when you hid it stay, without the name, as the record of hidden names says. A removed device's names go {days} after you remove it, unless you link it again first, and all of them go when your account is deleted

entries.data: The names you hid on your dashboard, without the names themselves: for each one, the device and project key it named and when you hid it, so that computer turns the name off too and doesn't send it again
entries.kept: Until that computer turns the name off too, and {days} after you hid it at most. All of them go when your account is deleted

entries.data: Keyed hashes of the Hackatime project names you link to a program
entries.kept: Until you unlink the program

entries.data: Build days: for each day, counted in your time zone, your credited time at evidence levels A and B that reached this server in time to count, whether that made it a build day, and when that was decided; your weekly goal, whether you met it each week or a freeze covered the week, and the freezes you earned and used
entries.kept: While your account exists

entries.data: Devlogs you published: the text exactly as the preview showed it, whether it's labeled as made with AI help, which of your projects it belongs to, when you published it, and the random ID your computer gave it
entries.kept: Each one until you delete it, which deletes it from this server at once, or until you delete your account

entries.data: The badges you chose to show on your profile, as codes from a fixed list, each with the random ID your computer gave it
entries.kept: Each one until you remove it, which deletes it from this server at once, or until you delete your account

entries.data: Devlogs you deleted and badges you removed, without their text, their project or which badge it was: only the random ID your computer gave each one and when you removed it, so a computer of yours that missed the removal can't publish it again
entries.kept: {days} after you removed it. All of them go when your account is deleted

entries.data: Backups, only if you turn them on: your device key, locked with your recovery code, and encrypted copies of your ledger and vault
entries.kept: Until you turn backups off or delete your account. Backup segments older than {days} are deleted

entries.data: This server's continuous backup: a copy of its database that the storage provider keeps up to date within seconds. It isn't encrypted with a key of the operator's own, so the storage provider could read it
entries.kept: Anything deleted from the database stays in this copy for up to {days}

entries.data: This server's nightly backups: a copy of its database each night, encrypted before it leaves the server
entries.kept: Anything deleted from the database stays in these copies for up to {days}

entries.data: Your submissions: which program each one went to, and that program's ID for it or the random ID your computer gave it; whether you made it on the web or from a computer, and which one; the projects it covers, and the keys those projects had on each of your computers when you submitted; the start and end of each stretch of time it covers; the scoring version and parameter table it was frozen with; a random number that fixes which prompts get drawn, and its hash; whether your Hack Club account still needs its eligibility confirmed; and each step it went through, with its time
entries.kept: While your account exists. Withdrawing a submission doesn't delete this record

entries.data: What you reveal when you submit hours: the records behind them, the prompts drawn for review, and any risk flags
entries.kept: Until the spot-check window closes ({window}). You can delete any revealed item yourself, at once

entries.data: Reviewer decisions and the reasons for cuts, written without personal data
entries.kept: As long as the program's record of the submission exists in Hack Club's Unified DB

entries.data: The evidence access log: who opened your submitted evidence, and when. You can see it
entries.kept: 2 years

entries.data: Notes from an audit call. Calls are never recorded
entries.kept: As long as the decision they belong to

entries.data: After you delete your account: a minimal fraud record (your Hack Club Auth ID, the verdict, its date and a reason category)
entries.kept: For a period Hack Club sets, which isn't decided yet. The deletion report lists it as kept

entries.data: Day roots: one hash a day over every batch the server received, with a count of those batches, published in the public pairtime-witness repository. On a server few people use, that count shows how many batches they uploaded that day. The server's operator can leave day roots off
entries.kept: Permanently. They hold only hashes and that daily count
